scope: CPU raster module and native differential reference; the browser still depends on Skia. No full-browser or performance acceptance.

reference.linux: Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64, glibc 2.39, FreeType 2.13.2; pinned local static reference only

behavior: Canvas RGBA surfaces use the raster pipeline on Linux; native N32 scratch masks and image-filter content retain the legacy path.
Linux N32 is BGRA, macOS N32 is RGBA. SkBitmapDevice::createDevice forces N32 for image-filter layers, while ordinary saved layers retain the parent color type.
Image shader and sprite legacy eligibility follows the source and destination storage; mipmaps preserve this metadata.
Native platform libm is retained: atan2f(0,-1) differs by one float ULP between Apple libm and glibc. Arc and stroke references therefore have platform-native expected hashes.
diagnostics: Initial Linux module runs failed because macOS fixture hashes and legacy RGBA blitter assumptions were used on Linux. The final suites above pass after native capture and storage-policy fixes.

The first whole-driver Linux run stopped at random bitmap export 5069 (RGBA premultiplied sRGB, flipped and resized), byte 180: V 118, native 162. Bitmap export sampling remains a separate pending fix.
Removing the scale restriction from drop-shadow was tried and reverted: trial 5714 differs by one in two channels at a single pixel. It is not enabled by this change.
A macOS FreeType regression invocation incorrectly included CoreText-only golden fixtures; normal CoreText follow-up passes. Dedicated FreeType fixtures pass.
Focused Linux build-supervisor and publication-lease checks: 37 pass, 11 platform skips. This does not compile the browser.
